visualInspection.method: Actual view_image inspection of every full raster extent; JPEGs were rendered by the tool from 2752x1536 to 2048x1143, PNGs at 1600x900. All labels and formula panels were visually inspected; no image-generation or image edits were performed.

entries.observation: Two gas bottles show lower/higher temperature and mean translational kinetic energy; the formula 3 k_B T/2 is explicitly classical ideal gas and individual speeds are stated to differ.
Piston and vacuum-expansion panels contrast ideal reversibility and entropy generation; the label 'fully reversible' requires including surroundings when teaching.
Plus-sign first law uses work on system, heat input and a system boundary. All three symbols are labeled.
Total entropy inequality, reversible equality and irreversible positivity are displayed. Ideal pendulum symbol is illustrative; it is not a real reversibility experiment.
Three columns distinguish reversible, quasi-static and irreversible; friction, finite temperature difference and free expansion are shown. Text must clarify that slow alone is insufficient.
Two panels distinguish an energy balance from spontaneous hot-to-cold direction; no entropy numerical calculation is shown.
Reversible substitute path shares endpoints A and B; integral and Q_rev warning are visible. Dashed real p-V path is schematic, not proof of equilibrium throughout.
No visualization in the bound page context. No raster inspection claimed.
Reservoir 500 J / 250 K = 2.0 J/K and transition 334 kJ / 273 K ≈ 1.22 kJ/K are correct; total transition heat is given in joules.
Isothermal expansion shows equal particle counts at increased volume, constant T, nR ln(V2/V1) and positive entropy change.

Heat transfer 100 J from 600 K to 300 K gives -0.167 and +0.333 J/K, total about +0.17 J/K. Ice-like decoration on the 300-K reservoir could misleadingly suggest freezing rather than merely a relatively lower temperature.

Clausius integral inequalities are correctly displayed for reversible/irreversible cycles. Positive Q_c in the waste-heat caption is a magnitude convention, not the signed heat entering the working substance, and is not explicitly labeled as a magnitude.
All four mechanisms visible. Distinct gases are specified for mixing; expansion removes an internal divider while preserving the outer vessel. Entropy transport is separated from generation.
Three distinct pictured position arrangements all have two particles on each side. These are simplified positional examples; momenta of a full classical microstate are not represented.
The N=4 microstate table lists 1,4,6,4,1 states and its six balanced strings are distinct. Near-balance for large N must not be confused with certain exact equality.
Eight particles are preserved; fixed N, equal T, unchanged momentum contribution, V^N multiplicity, logarithm derivation and R=N_A k_B are visible and consistent.
Picture explicitly uses work by the gas and ΔU=Q-W, correctly yielding 500-200=300 J. This differs from the prerequisite's work-on-system notation; it is an explicitly declared equivalent convention.
Isolated whole, signed reservoir changes and positive Q(1/Tc-1/Th) are explicit; text permits a subsystem's entropy decrease and describes the reverse as sole effect.
Two reservoirs, heat rejection, efficiency and Carnot limit are visible; 1-300/600=0.50 is correct. Heat flows use positive magnitudes, with work output in the balance.
Measured-data example gives 350/1000=0.35 and 1-300/600=0.50. No measurement uncertainty is depicted; the independent evidence task must still assess it.
